title: Halogenation: a trap for NLO enhancement in benzooxadiazole dithienosilole hybrids: a CDFT/TD-DFT investigation
content: To rationally design efficient nonlinear optical (NLO) materials, it is essential to understand the electronic structure and charge-transfer dynamics of materials, both of which are controlled by substituent effects. We investigated 10 benzo[c][1,2,5]oxadiazole-dithienosilole hybrids (WA-1 to WA-4 and WA-CN) and their C2 conformers with the help of DFT, conceptual DFT and TD-DFT in gas, toluene and water phases. C2 conformers were explicitly included to see whether the trends for the substituents changed if the mirror plane was lost. The HOMO–LUMO gap in the Cs series, which was 2.28 eV for WA-1 to 2.53 eV for WA-4, was widened monotonically by halogenation. In the C2 series, the gap is widened (2.23–2.48 eV), and in the cyano derivative WA-CN–C2, the gap is the smallest (2.08 eV). The intensity of the visible absorption bands was predicted by TD-DFT to be dominated by HOMO-to-LUMO transitions, and the order of the shift was systematically shifted towards the blue (WA-1 < WA-2 < WA-3 < WA-4) with a significant bathochromic effect for CN (f = 1.46). Dynamic hyper-Rayleigh scattering yielded values of βHRS up to 9468 a.u. (WA-1), with octupolar contributions dominating, while the values at 1456 nm were near-resonance (2ω = 728 nm), and interpreted accordingly. Third-order hyperpolarizability decreased as WA-1 (4.00 × 106 a.u.) > WA-2 (3.86 × 106 a.u.) > WA-3 (3.38 × 106 a.u.) > WA-4 (2.89 × 106 a.u). Second- and third-order responses were governed by different substituent orderings, and we demonstrated that this stemmed from the different tensorial origins of βtot and γ, namely the charge transfer efficiency and the transition dipole moment for the former, and the density of low-lying excited states and the spatial extent of the polarizable π-cloud for the latter. The reduced NLO response could be attributed to gap widening, localization of charge at halogen sites, and decreased orbital overlap for larger halogens. All compounds performed well when compared with the benchmarks of urea and p-nitroaniline, but halogenation remained detrimental in this context.
